tech.summary: GTA VI is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases in history when it comes out on November 19. Its immediate predecessor is the best-selling nonmobile game of all time. The game's release is causing other entertainment companies to delay products until next year because they know GTA VI will suck up the planet's attention for most of November. It will almost certainly be the most expensive video game ever created. This article looks at how Rockstar Games built what is expected to be the biggest video game blockbuster of all time.

tech.summary: Anthropic told investors recently that the company's revenue for the third quarter jumped about 45% from the prior quarter to $16.8 billion. The AI lab is currently pursuing what may become the largest-ever initial public offering. Its IPO could value the company at $2 trillion. tech.title: 28 Miles and Counting: NASA's Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record
tech.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has now driven 28.1 miles on Mars' surface, surpassing the distance that Opportunity covered from 2004 to 2018. Perseverance landed on Mars in February 2021 and has been traveling in and around the Jezero Crater since. It was set to surpass the driving record back in August, but it came across some interesting rocks, so it dawdled for two months. Perseverance most likely still has many miles to go in the coming years. This article contains some of the highlights from its drive so far.

tech.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
tech.summary: Two NASA missions are on track to launch to Venus in the early 2030s. The Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging (DAVINCI), which will send a parachute-assisted descent probe through Venus' atmosphere, is now scheduled for launch in December 2030. The Venus Emissivity, Radio science, InSAR, Topography, And Spectroscopy (VERITAS) mission will launch in November 2032 to map the Venusian surface by radar from orbit. The European Space Agency is building an orbiter for launch to Venus in 2032, and Rocket Lab plans to launch a privately funded probe as soon as next year to search for signs of organic material in the planet's clouds.

tech.title: State of Product reveals what AI still hasn't solved
tech.summary: 99% of product teams have fully integrated AI into at least one workflow. As AI becomes part of everyday work, it's expanding what PMs, designers, and engineers can do and changing how they work together. Atlassian's State of Product 2027 explores what comes after adoption, from broader roles to harder choices about where teams should focus. Read the report

tech.title: Code you didn't write
tech.summary: Being able to tell clean code from messy code is still useful, but it's becoming something that tools can help with. Knowing what shape a program should have before anyone writes it is something AI still can't do yet. The best way to get better at AI coding might be to spend more time thinking about problems and less time thinking about prompts. The programmers that get the most out of these tools already knew what they wanted.

tech.title: Agentic Verification
tech.summary: Giving AI agents a way to independently verify their work heavily improves the quality of output. Write end-to-end tests that simulate real user flows and act as the ground truth. Use property-based testing to specify what should never happen and generate thousands of test cases that attempt to break those constraints. Require tests to run quickly and deterministically so that agents retry when the loop is slow or unreliable.

webdev.title: The Most Common Questions About Agent Evals, Answered
webdev.summary: Agent evals score runs against desired behaviors, but exact-output tests often fail because agent outputs and paths vary. The guide recommends starting with 10 to 20 examples drawn from traces, combining code evaluators with LLM judges and human review, and using offline and online evals at different stages.

webdev.title: Lazy Loading Images and Media: How Far Ahead Browsers Fetch
webdev.summary: Browsers fetch lazy-loaded media at different distances, with Chrome adjusting its margin based on connection speed, Firefox using a fixed 600-pixel threshold, and Safari applying a viewport-based threshold to images. The article explains why the largest contentful paint image should load eagerly and why media dimensions should be reserved to prevent layout shifts. Its practical takeaway is to use native lazy loading selectively, based on how far ahead each browser fetches.

webdev.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
webdev.summary: GitHub rebuilt its star-history API to return up to 30 weeks of daily counts in one request. Maintainers can track a project's momentum without exposing stargazer identities, which could be scraped for spam or phishing. To avoid simply shifting the cost to count queries, the endpoint filters stars by time before counting, reducing database work.

webdev.title: Pure UI in the Agentic Era
webdev.summary: The article revisits the idea that UI should be a pure function of state and explains why it matters for agent-written interfaces. Passing roles, plans, billing status, and feature flags explicitly lets teams render and inspect each state combination before release.

webdev.title: Passkeys Are Not a Trap
webdev.summary: Synced consumer passkeys generally return no attestation, and WebAuthn attestation identifies an authenticator model rather than a user's operating system, browser, or firmware. The response argues that passkeys remain more phishing-resistant than TOTP and recommends continuing to use them.

webdev.title: AI agents and assistants are spending real money. Are you still blocking them?
webdev.summary: AI agents and assistants now browse, buy, and fetch content for users, so “block all bots” policies end up blocking business. webdev.title: OpenCode 2.0

It also adds background tasks and subagents, expands the plugin system, and includes breaking changes for 1.0 plugins and the server API.

data.title: Efficient search with OLTP
data.summary: Put the duct tape away. You don't have to tack on a standalone search engine to your database to solve your AI-agent-scale search problem. Lakebase Postgres now has a fast, scalable and serverless built-in search engine. Separating storage from compute means you don't have to keep your entire search index in RAM just to keep queries fast. Compute scales with actual search activity, while your index stays in lower-cost storage. Instead of chaining together multiple APIs for vector search, keyword search and filtering, you can do it all in one SQL query, against the same live operational data. Quench your need for Postgres speed Start building

data.title: CASTLE: training natural language search before the first real query
data.summary: Cold-start natural-language search often lacks both real queries and relevance labels. Airbnb's CASTLE jointly generates synthetic queries and labels from de-identified booking sessions. Its queries matched real guest query patterns much better than baselines, and human reviewers agreed with its relevance labels >90% of the time. Carefully governed behavioral data can bootstrap search training before meaningful traffic exists.

data.title: Turning Opportunistic AI Inference Capacity Into Better Ads Recommendations
data.summary: Meta uses idle computing capacity to improve ad recommendations by ranking more ads or routing requests to more powerful models. When that capacity disappears, the system quickly scales back this extra work while protecting normal service speed and reliability.

data.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
data.summary: GitHub built a star history API that returns daily counts without exposing users' identities, cutting React's full history from about 2,500 requests to 24. It reduces database work by filtering stars by date before counting them, rather than repeatedly processing every star.

data.title: Zero-downtime Postgres upgrades with logical replication
data.summary: Logical replication offers a practical path to near-zero-downtime PostgreSQL major upgrades, with live rollback enabled by reverse replication. A Docker-based demonstration ran old and new clusters in parallel, freezing writes and waiting for replication to catch up before cutover. It achieved 181 ms of write interruption during upgrade and 179 ms during rollback, without data loss.

data.title: Need to Know: Implementing row-level security for Claude Dashboards via Model Context Protocol
data.summary: This proof of concept shows how to add row-level security to Claude Dashboards using an MCP server to authenticate users and query DuckDB for only the data they can access. Access rules are enforced before data reaches Claude, allowing the same dashboard to show different results for each user.

data.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
data.summary: Cloudflare held back exponential hardware growth by shrinking data earlier and moving duplication later: split monolithic schemas, switch to zstd, send each event once then replicate after sampling, sample at the edge, and pre-aggregate known queries. Optimize bytes, not just compute: prune fields, compress measured workloads, push reductions upstream, and replicate compacted data.

data.title: Four PostgreSQL arguments that came out even
data.summary: PostgreSQL micro-optimization alternatives often don't matter. For 1,000 IDs, IN, ANY, and VALUES joins perform similarly; prefer parameterized ANY for stable query text. Short text, enums, and smallints use near-identical storage; mostly-NULL columns are cheap. Don't blindly rewrite but EXPLAIN on your own data.

data.title: Browse ready-made AI assets. Run on live data in minutes.
data.summary: Precisely AI Studio is a self-serve library of AI apps, agents, skills, prompts, and MCP connectors organized by industry and data domain. Connect to live, governed data and go from browsing to running in minutes. Try it free, no commitment, no strings. Try AI Studio free See what's inside

data.title: Phoenix
data.summary: Phoenix is a self-hosted, open-source AI observability platform for tracing, evaluating, and debugging LLM applications. It captures OpenTelemetry traces; offers retrieval and response evaluations, versioned datasets, and experiments; and supports prompt testing and replay. Framework- and provider-agnostic instrumentation makes it useful for teams that need to diagnose agent behavior and measure changes before production.

data.title: XERJ
data.summary: XERJ is an Apache-2.0, Elasticsearch-compatible local search engine that automatically indexes code, logs, PDFs, SQLite, and CSVs into typed datasets for agent retrieval, incident analysis, and RAG. Its autoindex workflow avoids schema setup and returns ranked passages with file and line locations. The project defaults to local operation, although optional reranking can send text to an external provider.

data.title: SQLBuild: safe refactoring for warehouse SQL
data.summary: SQLBuild is an open-source SQL and Python transformation framework for safely changing warehouses. It checks contracts and lineage before execution, runs graph-level tests and production diffs, and lets teams rename incremental models or columns while preserving history and compatibility views. A local DuckDB playground makes it easy to evaluate. Snowflake, Postgres, BigQuery, and Databricks adapters are available.

data.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
data.summary: Anthropic replaced Git with Scion, an in-house version control system built in five months, after daily code merges grew from 2,500 to over 30,000. By moving operations to servers and fetching only the files needed, it reports roughly 100 times faster checkouts and 200 times lower CPU and memory requirements than its previous Git mirror infrastructure.

data.title: Parsing JSON at tens of gigabytes per second… in Python
data.summary: Daniel Lemire's benchmark processed 7.6 GB of JSON in about 0.12 seconds using fastsimdjson on free-threaded Python across 64 cores, reaching roughly 66 GB/s. The speed comes from running threads in parallel and creating Python objects only for the fields needed, with data already decompressed in memory.

data.title: Jev handed our LLM the wrong page a tenth as often as our embeddings
data.summary: Jev picked the right page first 88% of the time (vs. 70% for embedding search) across 168 test questions, and cut irrelevant results to the AI receptionist from 33% to 3% by answering "none" when no page fit.

data.title: What gets TOASTed in Postgres
data.summary: Postgres's TOAST compresses large values or moves them to a separate table.

design.title: Getty Images to go private after restructuring deal
design.summary: Getty Images is planning a prepackaged Chapter 11 filing and will go private, backed by up to $533 million from the Getty family and Koch Equity Development. The deal follows a collapsed $3.7 billion Shutterstock merger and leaves the company, carrying over $1.3 billion in debt, wholly family- and Koch-owned. Generative AI image tools keep squeezing the stock-licensing business of both Getty and Shutterstock.

design.title: AI Agent Developer Manus Raises $500M+ at Reported $4B Valuation
design.summary: Manus has raised more than $500 million in a round led by Boyu Capital, with Tencent participating, at a reported $4 billion valuation. That figure roughly doubles Meta's reported offer, an acquisition Chinese regulators blocked in April. The newly released Manus 2.0 cuts token use by 23.2% on some tasks and adds Cloud Computer and Cue.

design.title: iOS 27.2 beta 4 removes Apple's redesigned Health app and brings back the old design
design.summary: Apple has removed its redesigned Health app from iOS 27.2 beta 4, restoring the existing interface after allowing testers to try the overhaul in earlier betas. The redesign introduced features including Insights, Longevity, Health Age, and readiness metrics, but Apple had already indicated that it would arrive separately later in 2026. Data collected while testing the new version remains available through Settings, suggesting the redesign has been delayed rather than abandoned.

design.title: On what a clean interface hides
design.summary: Minimal interfaces can reduce visible complexity while quietly transferring more work to users, who must discover hidden controls, interpret ambiguous icons, and infer what happened after an action. Comparing a hidden bookmark icon with an explicit Save button demonstrates how adding labels, confirmation, and an Undo action can make an interface visually busier but cognitively simpler. Good interface design therefore requires balancing visual restraint with enough visible information to support newcomers, while potentially reducing that guidance as familiarity grows.

design.title: When code is no longer the constraint: Inside Anthropic's design team
design.summary: AI has accelerated engineering at Anthropic to the point where deciding what deserves to be built is becoming a greater constraint than implementing it, pushing designers closer to production code and working prototypes. Designers routinely build their own tools, generate interactive variations using Anthropic's design system, and collaborate through smaller, more frequent critiques and working demos rather than lengthy specifications. Technical fluency is increasingly useful, but Anthropic also values designers who continually reinvent their workflows, have a point of view about where software is heading, and can move fluidly between strategic direction and hands-on making.

design.title: Emerging Patterns: Design Leadership in 2026
design.summary: Research involving 119 design leaders found 93 distinct routes into the profession, with fewer than 30% having studied in dedicated design programs and nearly 40% beginning their careers elsewhere. Traditional career ladders are giving way to more diversified portfolio careers, while 94% of respondents expect their tool stacks to change dramatically over the next five years as AI transforms design work. The qualities that appear most durable amid this uncertainty are not technical skills but intuition, navigation, adaptability, resilience, and stewardship, including a growing commitment among established designers to mentor the next generation.

design.title: Refined UI Components with Satisfying Hover
design.summary: Open Source UI components built on a design philosophy where every animation serves a functional purpose — motion is information, not decoration.

design.title: The Missing Foundation for AI-Generated Websites

design.title: Build Your Own Design Apps with AI
design.summary: Toolcraft is an open-source starter kit and UI library for building custom design apps with AI. Use it to create branded asset generators, explore new visual styles, and turn repetitive design tasks into reusable tools.

design.title: Thumbnails Give a Fast Overview
design.summary: Thumbnails let people choose by looking rather than reading, because a scene's gist registers in about a tenth of a second. They fail when neighbors look identical or a preview misrepresents the click, so the two rules are: differ from your neighbors, and resemble your destination. Fourteen guidelines follow, along with the risks AI brings when it selects, personalizes, or synthesizes previews.

design.title: How two simple dots gave Pictoplasma a fresh personality for 2026
design.summary: andstudio transformed Pictoplasma's deliberately neutral identity around the positioning “Never faceless,” giving the character-design festival its own personality without competing with the work it showcases. A customized version of Lift Type's Melun adds a glyph containing two dots that function as eyes, allowing typography itself to become a character through pareidolia while colors and layouts change between festival editions. The same two-dot device extends into motion, print, installations, tattoos, and guerrilla applications, creating a playful system simple enough to work within the festival's limited budget.

design.title: Experience Planes – The Big 4: Who, What, Where, and Why of Experiences
design.summary: Picking a single lens such as customer, shopping, or brand experience quietly shapes a design conversation before any design begins. Four experience planes widen the view: who is involved, what they are doing, where it happens, and why the organization offers it. Five examples, from license renewal to food delivery, show frustration often sitting in the connections between places.

design.title: André Britz draws dimly remembered landscapes, in a book held together with a pink elastic band
design.summary: André Britz's Gone with the Clouds collects intuitive landscapes drawn entirely from memory in a 64-page publication whose loose pages and pink elastic binding deliberately remain changeable, mirroring how memories blur, shift, and rearrange themselves over time.

design.title: The chaotic Apple HomeView ad is stressful viewing
design.summary: Apple's HomeView launch ad depicts a chaotic family morning, with the shared smart-home display handling messages, entertainment, and home controls.

marketing.title: Social Media and Wellbeing: It's Complicated
marketing.summary: Moderate social media use is associated with better well-being than either low or high use, though differences are generally small. 81% of adults used social media in the past week, rising to 95% among ages 15-29. High use of 2 or more hours daily is linked to more anger, loneliness, and sadness. 47% of young adults are high users compared with 12% of adults aged 50+. High use is also associated with lower life evaluations than moderate use in high-income countries, but not elsewhere.

marketing.title: TikTok Inks Second Major Microdrama Deal, Partners With Made By Us Studios
marketing.summary: TikTok's first microdrama partnership, with Issa Rae's Hoorae Media, produced Screen Time, which has pulled nearly 580 million views since April. The new deal shifts the focus to creators, with the production arm of management company Made By All co-producing vertical series built around talent that already has an audience, for both TikTok and its PineDrama app.

marketing.title: Your AI agents sound generic because their context is a mess
marketing.summary: AI agents produce generic outputs when their context is poorly organized, not because they need better prompts or models. To improve results, separate context into 3 layers. Keep brand voice and audience profiles in a lean knowledge base. Store transcripts and playbooks in a searchable library that retrieves relevant passages on demand. Fetch changing metrics like traffic and pipeline directly from APIs. Map recurring questions to their data sources before building workflows, remove outdated content, and assign owners to maintain accuracy.

marketing.title: Use Google AI Mode to Find Content Gaps
marketing.summary: Use Google AI Mode to identify content gaps on local service pages. Search for a service with a city name and review the follow-up questions to understand what information Google considers relevant when matching customers with businesses. Interview the business owner about their services, pricing, and processes, then add those original insights to service pages to answer customer questions and give AI context competitors can't easily replicate.

marketing.title: How to Turn Your SaaS Pricing Page Into a First 30 Days Conversion Tool
marketing.summary: Trial users revisit a SaaS pricing page several times in their first 30 days, and each visit asks something different, from whether the product is a serious option to what an upgrade unlocks right now. Build the page for repeat scrutiny with a full plan-comparison table and trust signals. Keep one price framing synced across banners, emails, and checkout. Hold upgrade pitches until users have made something, then spread them out rather than stacking them in the trial's last 48 hours.

marketing.title: Your website could be a conversational AI experience
marketing.summary: Your visitors have questions. Instead of making them hunt for answers, CrafterQ gives them a conversation with an AI agent trained on your website, docs, and FAQs. See how it can guide your visitors to the next step: demo, quote, or purchase. Try it for free

marketing.title: Brand Consistency That Converts (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Learn how to audit your brand's representation in AI search and create consistent on-brand content at scale. The 60-minute webinar also covers turning email signatures into targeted campaigns using HubSpot audience segments. It will take place on October 20 at 9 AM ET.

marketing.title: “You didn't do it right”
marketing.summary: Frameworks like OKRs can fail when they don't fit a company's culture, team dynamics, or existing processes, even when implemented correctly. After four failed attempts at OKRs, WP Engine found success with a metrics framework that let teams choose goals they personally valued and could directly control. Teams started with one metric for a quarter, then added one or two more based on what they learned. Rather than rolling out a framework company-wide, test it with one team, gather feedback, and adapt it or try another approach if it does not work.

marketing.title: We Now Know the #1 Ranking Factor for AI and LLMs, The Data
marketing.summary: Contextually relevant backlinks had the strongest correlation with AI rankings across 17 AI search channels. For GPT-6 Astra, the correlation averaged 0.57 across industries and was positive in all 100. Unlinked brand mentions also correlated with rankings at 0.41 compared with 0.55 for total backlinks. The findings suggest prioritizing links and coverage from relevant industry sources over simply increasing backlink volume.

marketing.title: How Saie Beauty became the global powerhouse everyone's talking about
marketing.summary: Saie builds products around specific needs it spots in public, then uses how the product came about as the marketing story. Its Bellini eyeshadow was developed in its Italian lab with a creator whose followers had watched her test over 50 shades in three years, while its City Set spray was named after the Knicks dancers and led to an official team partnership. The approach shows up in how consumers see the brand, with 53% saying Saie meets their needs against a 43% category average.

crypto.title: BitMEX Sued in UK for Return of $27M BTC Over Unlicensed Derivatives
crypto.summary: A British software engineer has filed suit against BitMEX operator HDR Global Trading in London's Commercial Court, seeking return of 324.8 BTC (~$27.2M) on the grounds that BitMEX conducted regulated derivatives activity in the UK without FCA authorization. The claim, filed under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, targets 1,053 losing perpetual swap trades across five accounts from 2018 to 2022, arguing those contracts are unenforceable against UK residents who dealt with an unauthorized firm. A deceit claim accompanies the restitution suit, alleging BitMEX knew it lacked authorization while representing to clients it could lawfully trade with them. Barber's legal team at Seladore Legal suggests other UK users entered similar contracts, putting total potential exposure at hundreds of millions of pounds, with BitMEX having closed operations on September 23.

crypto.title: Strive Buys 3k Bitcoin for $280M, Now Fifth-Largest Corporate Holder
crypto.summary: Strive acquired 3,311 BTC between October 5 and 9 for $280M at an average of ~$84,500, bringing its total treasury to 32,773 BTC and ranking it fifth among publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holders. The purchase was financed through its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock (SATA), alongside a $208M warrant exercise, with cash reserves growing to $310.3M through the period. Bitcoin holdings expanded 11.2% against a 9.4% rise in effective common share count, benefiting existing shareholders on a per-BTC basis. CEO Matt Cole has targeted second-largest public corporate holder by year-end, though Strive currently trails Metaplanet by 11,227 BTC.

crypto.title: Agent-Native Elixir Stack With x402 Payments and WebMCP
crypto.summary: Regents Labs released an open-source Elixir/Phoenix/Ash stack for building agent-native applications, bundling WebMCP for exposing page tools to AI agents, SIWA for agent-specific authentication and sybil resistance, and x402 stablecoin payments for monetizing agent interactions. The stack separates agent and human identity layers, with Privy handling shared human accounts across five production sites already running the architecture. An open-source bootstrapping template called ash-template lets developers spin up compatible apps with payments, compute, and identity pre-wired, with Elixir chosen over TypeScript/React for cost and horizontal scaling at agent volumes. The platform distributes all revenue from its five properties to $REGENT token stakers, operating without VC backing.

crypto.title: Rain Launches Embedded Stablecoin Wallets, Files for OCC National Trust Charter
crypto.summary: Rain launched embedded stablecoin wallets supporting USDC, USDT, and other assets across 12 chains, including Base and Solana, paired with Rain-issued Visa and Mastercard cards accepted at 175 million merchant locations and USD payouts to 80+ countries. The launch follows Rain's acquisition of stored-value platform Ansa two months ago and an OCC national trust bank charter filing eight days prior, moves that shift the customer relationship away from third-party wallet infrastructure providers like Dynamic, Privy, and Turnkey. Rain's full stack spans card processing via Lithic, Episode Six, and Paymentology, direct Visa and Mastercard scheme memberships via Puerto Rico, and receivables financing through Credit Coop. An approved OCC charter would unlock custody monetization on top of a model that combines stablecoin rails with traditional finance licenses to function as a full-service card issuer.

crypto.title: Pair Tokens: Auto-Compounding ERC-20 LP Positions via Uniswap v4 Hooks
crypto.summary: StonkBrokers introduced Pair Tokens, a new ERC-20 primitive built on Uniswap v4 hooks that fuses two underlying assets into a single fungible token representing a full-range liquidity pool position. Unlike standard LP NFTs, Pair Tokens auto-compound through a permissionless compound function that reinvests accumulated trading fees back into the position, removing the need for manual fee harvesting. The ERC-20 format preserves composability, allowing Pair Tokens to be traded onchain, LPed, or integrated with launchpads, while a 10% fee on compounded LP fees funds $STONKBROKER token buybacks. Minting and redeeming are live on Robinhood Chain via the StonkBrokers platform as of October 13.

crypto.title: The Death of the Interface
crypto.summary: Capable LLMs and stablecoin legislation enacted on two continents (the US GENIUS Act, effective January, and Europe's MiCA, now in full force) have converged. As AI agents displace app-based interfaces, today's payment infrastructure breaks down because its risk stack (authentication, fraud, disputes, and liability) assumes a human completing each transaction step, a premise that fails entirely in agent-to-agent commerce. David Marcus proposes "headless money" as the required fix: a stablecoin-settled, API-only payment layer combining embedded wallets, fiat connectivity, and card networks that agents can call without any frontend. Lightspark, which he leads, is building toward this stack, with the commercial logic that whoever controls agent-mediated purchase decisions captures marketplace-level economics rather than the 1-300 bps of a conventional payment rail.

crypto.title: Aave V4 deposits are concentrated in partner-built hubs
crypto.summary: About 59% of deposits in Aave's new V4 markets sit in three partner-focused hubs (EtherFi Cash, Global Dollar, and Coinbase Stocks), together holding about $409M of the roughly $695M across 10 new markets. EtherFi's Cash hub alone holds $311.5M, nearly 45% of Q3 V4 deposits, and the DAO gets 20% of its revenue with no operating costs. Sentora has proposed a similar curated structure with a 50/50 revenue split, pending governance approval.

crypto.title: Prediction Market Data Ranks F1 as the Most Dramatically Volatile Sport
crypto.summary: Dragonfly Capital managing partner Haseeb Qureshi applied prediction market data to rank sports by drama, measuring minute-by-minute odds volatility as the metric for suspense rather than scoreboard activity. The methodology treats real drama as outcome probabilities shifting in real-time, discounting action that does not move win probability. F1 ranked first, followed by CS2, soccer, basketball, tennis, American football, and baseball, with golf last by a wide margin. The framework demonstrates prediction markets as a quantitative layer for analyzing real-world phenomena, well beyond their primary use in financial price discovery.

crypto.title: AI agents that save or make people money
crypto.summary: A major consumer fintech opportunity is agents that negotiate medical bills, rent, and interest rates, optimize card rewards, find benefits, and cancel subscriptions.

crypto.title: Crypto cards grew up to 108x in a year
crypto.summary: Total crypto card spend tripled from $403M in September 2025 to a record $1.22B this September.

crypto.title: Kraken's parent Payward is buying Lithuania's Saldo Bank
crypto.summary: Payward (Kraken and Krak) will buy Saldo Bank, with closing expected in 2027 pending regulatory approval.

crypto.title: How to win in consumer crypto
crypto.summary: Winning consumer crypto apps survive market cycles by managing burn, building a defensible moat, thinking in years rather than token launches, and building distribution into the product through viral loops.

it.title: 10 infrastructure connectivity mistakes you don't want to learn the hard way
it.summary: Building across clouds and data centers gets complicated fast. Routing, resilience, egress costs, automation, security, provider choices. There's a lot that can get messy. Megaport's guide breaks down 10 common infrastructure connectivity mistakes IT teams make when designing and operating hybrid and multicloud environments — from treating the network as an afterthought to overlooking redundancy, data movement costs, and provider lock-in. See what can go wrong, why it matters, and what to do instead to build a network that's more resilient, scalable, and ready for what comes next.

it.title: US tech giants warn Europe that ditching US tech giants could cost €115B
it.summary: A study commissioned by a US technology industry group estimates that European cloud sovereignty policies could impose €115 billion in costs over a decade. The findings reflect modeled scenarios rather than established costs, highlighting the competing arguments around digital independence, vendor choice, and the economics of cloud infrastructure.

it.title: Internet traffic records topple as Champions League returns
it.summary: European internet exchanges recorded major traffic spikes as Champions League matches resumed, with DE-CIX Frankfurt reaching a reported 21.47 Tbps. The new records demonstrate how live streaming continues to push network capacity, traffic engineering, and infrastructure resilience.

it.title: SAP customers seek renewed control over their ERP fate
it.summary: SAP customers are pushing back on cloud migration pressure, asking for more flexibility, predictable licensing, and continued support for hybrid and on-premises ERP deployments. With many organizations still running older SAP systems ahead of the 2027 support deadline, the debate highlights growing tensions between vendor roadmaps and enterprise technology strategies.

it.title: The Rise of DeployCos
it.summary: AI labs, hyperscalers, and incumbent consultancies are increasingly establishing specialized deployment companies—or DeployCos—to embed forward-deployed engineers directly inside enterprises. These entities help bridge the "diffusion gap" or "capability overhang" by assisting organizations with custom workflow integration, systems access, and organizational change management.

it.title: Chasing that 32 ms tail latency in ClickHouse
it.summary: Engineers at ClickHouse investigated why simple SELECT queries experienced an unexpected 32 ms tail latency after idle periods on high-RTT networks. They discovered that unbatched metadata packets sent alongside result data quickly exhausted the TCP congestion window after it had been reset to its initial size during idleness. To resolve the issue, ClickHouse implemented application-level batching for these metadata packets, effectively halving the TCP segment count and eliminating the tail latency penalty.

it.title: AI is pretty much everywhere... and so is shadow AI
it.summary: AI is running in 94.9% of organizations. No surprise there. But Field Effect telemetry also finds signs of shadow AI in 88.1% of them. Unseen and ungoverned, AI use creates a threat surface that grows with every new tool that's deployed. Learn to govern AI use without blocking all of it.

it.title: Firefox takes aim at the enterprise browser market
it.summary: Mozilla is introducing Firefox Enterprise with centralized policy management, security controls, and a self-hostable administration console. Initially targeting four European countries, the offering gives organizations another managed browser option, particularly those seeking more infrastructure control and less dependence on Chromium.

it.title: Shopify Is Widening the Catalog Door to Personal Agents. The Sign-Off Stays Human
it.summary: Shopify is expanding its catalog access to shopper-configured personal agents while keeping a mandatory human sign-off on every purchase. The company's new Agentic Storefronts provide merchants out-of-the-box access to tools like ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Gemini, allowing billions of products to be discovered and purchased directly through agent conversations.

it.title: Workday makes Sana its interface, launches Agent Harness, decision, and work intelligence
it.summary: Workday announced at Workday Rising that it has made Sana the primary front-door interface for its platform and launched Agent Harness to let enterprises build secure AI agents for finance and HR data. The company also introduced ambient agents like the Talent Acquisition Agent, Workday Decision Intelligence, and Workday Work Intelligence. CEO Aneel Bhusri stated that Workday is refounding itself around artificial intelligence with a startup mindset.

it.title: SolarWinds launches Avior AI agents to automate network operations
it.summary: SolarWinds has introduced Avior AI agents designed to investigate network issues, identify configuration drift, and assist with incident remediation across enterprise environments. The platform supports varying levels of automation, from human-approved actions to autonomous workflows with auditability and safeguards.

it.title: Cisco, Nvidia team up to build fatter, faster pluggable
it.summary: Cisco and Nvidia have proposed a new optical transceiver form factor capable of supporting up to 12.8 Tbps of bandwidth. The design promises higher density and improved power efficiency for future data center networks, although commercial deployments remain ahead.

it.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
it.summary: To handle massive scaling challenges caused by AI-generated code that merged 30,000 changes daily, Anthropic built an in-house version control system called Scion and fully migrated its monorepo from git in five months. The company designed Scion around the assumption that clients are always online, implementing a centralized server architecture, horizontal scalability, server-side commits, and sparse checkouts. This new infrastructure reduced CPU and memory requirements by 200x compared to their previous git mirroring setup and accelerated CI code checkouts from minutes to seconds.

it.title: Ultra Ethernet 1.1 extends the specification to scale-up networks and adds programmable congestion control
it.summary: The latest Ultra Ethernet specification introduces networking improvements designed to support larger computing clusters and more sophisticated congestion management.

it.title: Developer guide to Gemini 4 Argon Long Decode
it.summary: Google has introduced Long Decode for the Gemini 4 Argon model, enabling completions up to 1 million tokens long by splitting generation across multiple model inferences.
